question.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{x}{4},\,1<x<3
$$

Given that $\text{E}[X]=\frac{13}{6},$ compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}+6X+2].$

*Hint: You may assume that $\text{E}[aX+bY]=a\text{E}[X]+b\text{E}[Y]$ for any random variables $X$ and $Y$ and constants $a$ and $b.$*
question.worked_solution:
First, we simplify using the hint and the properties of expected value:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}+6X+2] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]+6\text{E}[X]+\text{E}[2] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]+6\text{E}[X]+2\end{aligned}
$$

For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ the $n$th raw moment of $X$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{n}]={\int }_{S}{x}^{n}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

We already know $\text{E}[X].$ So, we compute the second raw moment of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{S}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{x}{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{{x}^{3}}{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{4}}{16}\,|}_{1}^{3} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\text{E}[X]=\frac{13}{6}$ and $\text{E}[{X}^{2}]=5$ into the simplified expression, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}+6X+2] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]+6\text{E}[X]+2 \\  & =5+6\cdot \frac{13}{6}+2 \\  & =5+13+2 \\  & =20.\end{aligned}
$$
